The orchestra has voted to keep the soundtrack digital.

cutter.text: The kitchen has developed an industrial process for shaping things that will be eaten immediately.
A tool with the manufacturing cost of several batches of cookies.
The bakery has survived centuries without importing a CAD model.
A precision instrument for giving dough a temporary identity.

stamp.text: The postal service has been informed of an unnecessary rival.
A miniature printing press produced by another printing press because apparently one wasn't enough.
The ink has been given an elaborate administrative assistant.
An expensive way to leave the same mark repeatedly.

frame.text: The photograph has been given a border with a larger operating budget than the camera.
An exhibition space for evidence that you used to have other hobbies.
The wall has a new reason to demand structural compensation.
The picture is finally being displayed in a monument to everything that came after it.

shelf.text: The clutter has successfully negotiated an expansion of its territory.
That shelf is an investment in all the things you haven't printed yet.
The storage crisis has been addressed by creating more storage crisis infrastructure.
The furniture is now legally an accomplice to the hobby.

cap.text: You have manufactured a lid for something that once had a perfectly good lid.
A very expensive solution to an object having an exposed end.
The bottle has received a small but deeply bureaucratic roof.
The cap is a tiny monument to the original missing part.

plug.text: The hole has been informed that its services are no longer required.
An elaborate solution to the scandal of empty space.
The opening has been closed following a lengthy procurement process.
You have produced a physical manifestation of the phrase nothing to see here.

cover.text: The original design has been placed under a layer of plausible deniability.
A concealment strategy with its own material invoice.
The imperfections now have private accommodation.
An expensive blanket for an object that has never experienced embarrassment.

lid.text: The container has acquired a ceiling and a whole new budget.
The contents have been sentenced to indefinite detention.
A hat for a box, because apparently the box had social ambitions.
The lid represents a major achievement in the science of closing things.

spinner.text: The object has reached the highest level of productivity available to a circle.
A tiny machine designed to spend its entire career going nowhere.
The industrial revolution has officially run out of serious problems.
Your desk now has its own miniature economy of wasted momentum.

ring.text: The jewelry industry would like to remind you that plastic is not an investment strategy.
A symbolic commitment to spending money on a machine that makes circles.
The engagement announcement has been delayed pending a material change.
That ring has the resale prospects of a used zip tie.

coin.text: The central bank has declined to recognize the filament standard.
Your printer has discovered a currency that costs more to make than it is worth.
A monetary system backed entirely by optimism and a heated bed.
Economists have been summoned to explain why this is not technically inflation.

token.text: A financial instrument with absolutely no chance of being accepted at a financial institution.
The arcade would like a word about your private mint.
You have minted a coin whose value is measured in explanations.
The exchange rate between plastic and regret remains unfavorable.

frog.text: Kermit would take one look and return to the swamp.
That frog has the ecological usefulness of a parking meter.
The amphibian's leap of faith apparently ended at the edge of the build plate.
Evolution gave it legs and your slicer gave it nowhere to go.

cat.text: A cat would knock this off a shelf and then demand you apologize.
Finally, a cat that isn't convinced your entire salary belongs to it.
Schrodinger would put it in a box and leave the outcome to customer support.
Even Garfield would find a way to charge you rent for its presence.

dog.text: A dog would eat this and somehow have a more productive afternoon.
The obedience school has graduated its first completely stationary student.
Man's best friend has been replaced by a monthly installment on a machine.
The mailman has downgraded the threat level to decorative.

owl.text: Athena sent a formal request to stop associating owls with wisdom.
The owl has mastered the art of looking judgmental without spending anything.
Harry Potter's postal service would classify this as a delivery exception.
The only thing nocturnal about it was the poor decision that started the print.

butterfly.text: Darwin would be disappointed by this interpretation of flight.
A caterpillar does the same transformation without filing an expense report.
The butterfly effect has apparently reached your credit card statement.
The ecosystem has acquired a decorative insect with no plans to pollinate.

rocket.text: NASA spent billions on launch vehicles and you cornered the stationary rocket market.
SpaceX would call this a successful static display and quietly disable the comments.
That rocket has a launch window lasting until your next house move.
The Apollo program got to the Moon with less drama than your slicer.

boat.text: The coast guard has downgraded this vessel to an office supply.
A naval fleet with a combined cruising range of zero nautical miles.
The maritime museum is politely declining donations from this particular shipyard.
The captain's log begins and ends with the electricity meter.

castle.text: Feudalism has returned, and the peasants are now paying in spools.
Your miniature kingdom has a more attainable housing market than the real one.
The castle has a moat made entirely of credit card statements.
Congratulations on becoming a landlord to a population of imaginary serfs.

house.text: The housing crisis has been solved for people approximately two inches tall.
A property developer would still try to sell this as a luxury starter home.
The mortgage broker has offered financing on the filament alone.
The open house will be held on the bookshelf.

tree.text: A forest that will survive longer than the actual forest used to package its filament.
The tree has outsourced photosynthesis to the electrical grid.
An environmental initiative that begins with buying more plastic.
The lumber industry is now competing with a nozzle.

guitar.text: Jimi Hendrix would probably ask whether the strings were sold separately.
An instrument whose most audible feature was its manufacturing process.
The guitar has already released its first album of complete silence.
The music store has been spared another customer asking about tonewood.

elephant.text: The elephant in the room is now the amount of money spent manufacturing an elephant.
Evolution perfected a trunk and you perfected a reason to buy gray filament.
The wildlife sanctuary has declined this particular adoption application.
An elephant never forgets, especially when you print the receipt next to it.

bear.text: The bear market has discovered a new way to consume disposable income.
That bear has been reassigned from apex predator to shelf ornament.
Goldilocks would have returned this one to the manufacturer.
The park ranger has issued a warning about feeding it more filament.

fox.text: The fox is supposed to be cunning, which makes the manufacturing budget especially awkward.
A woodland creature with no natural enemies except the vacuum cleaner.
The henhouse has upgraded its security level to mildly decorative.
Even a fox would know better than to pay retail for this.

rabbit.text: The rabbit population is multiplying at a rate your shelving cannot sustain.
Bugs Bunny would ask how this particular cartoon got funded.
The Easter Bunny has outsourced production to a remarkably expensive factory.
A creature famous for reproducing quickly is now subject to a slicer estimate.

penguin.text: Antarctica would like its wildlife returned in a more biodegradable format.
The penguin's natural habitat has been reduced to the shelf beside your keyboard.
The Linux mascot has requested a different department to handle hardware.
The tuxedo is the only part of this project that looks financially responsible.

whale.text: The whale has been promoted from marine mammal to endangered desk space.
Captain Ahab could have saved himself a lot of trouble with a smaller filament order.
The ocean's largest mammals would question this particular allocation of resources.
A whale whose entire migration route is between the printer and the shelf.

ghost.text: The paranormal activity here is the mysterious disappearance of your paycheck.
Even the ghost is embarrassed to haunt this particular piece of real estate.
A supernatural being whose only earthly attachment is the build plate.
Ghostbusters would bill the printer for wasting their time.

robot.text: Artificial intelligence has declined to be associated with this particular hardware.
Boston Dynamics is safe from competition for at least another decade.
The singularity has been rescheduled due to a shortage of functional parts.
Even the Roomba has a stronger claim to world domination.

mushroom.text: That mushroom has the nutritional value of the packaging it came in.
Mario wouldn't even jump for this one.
The fungus has achieved immortality at the expense of being useful to the ecosystem.
The forest floor has filed a complaint about the unauthorized development.

curiosity rover.text: NASA drove a rover on Mars while yours faces the hostile terrain of a desk.
The rover's mission is to search for intelligent spending decisions, with no findings so far.
Mars has declined the latest proposed addition to its surface debris.

eiffel tower.text: Paris spent two years building the original and you still managed to make it a financial inconvenience.
The French tourism board would prefer you keep this landmark at home.
An iconic symbol of Paris brought to you by an appliance with a questionable accent.

gyroid.text: Topology has finally achieved the commercial success of a disorganized sponge.
The mathematician responsible for this would like to discuss the cost of empty space.
A structure so complicated even the infill is having an identity crisis.

jukebox.text: The jukebox can now play every song except the sound of money returning to your account.
A retro music experience brought to you by a very modern electricity bill.
The diner has been closed since 1978 and somehow the jukebox is still costing money.

church bell.text: The bell tolls for another afternoon that could have been spent doing literally anything else.
The congregation has requested an audit of the offertory filament fund.
An expensive way to announce the arrival of absolutely nobody.

marionette.text: The puppet has achieved complete independence from the string and total dependence on the electricity company.
The theater department has requested a separate budget for bad dreams.
Even a puppet would ask who is pulling the strings on these spending decisions.

mammoth.text: The Ice Age ended and somehow your printer is still trying to resurrect it.
Paleontology has taken a sharp turn into expensive interior decorating.
The mammoth survived extinction in the form of yet another object that won't fit in a drawer.

dino.text: The asteroid ended the dinosaurs and your printer has decided to appeal the ruling.
Jurassic Park is now accepting auditions for a much lower budget sequel.
The fossil record is about to get a confusing new layer.

elf.text: Santa has outsourced his labor force to a machine that takes all day to produce one employee.
The North Pole's productivity figures are about to look rather embarrassing.
The elf on the shelf has finally received a competing claim to the shelf.

chameleon.text: A chameleon changes color for survival; yours does it because the purge tower has a gambling problem.
David Attenborough would narrate this as a rare example of camouflage failing to hide a receipt.
Nature gave it camouflage and you gave it the wardrobe budget of a Las Vegas residency.
The chameleon blends into every environment except a financially responsible household.
Somewhere a lizard changed color for free and ruined your entire sales pitch.

polymaker scientist.text: Einstein developed relativity without needing sixteen colors to explain his hair.
The scientist's first experiment tests how much purge waste one household can rationalize.
Oppenheimer split the atom; this laboratory specializes in splitting a spool into seventeen little piles.
Peer review rejected the paper but accepted the figure as a warning about grant spending.
The Nobel committee is still waiting for a discovery more significant than swapping filament.

duplo swing.text: LEGO built an empire selling plastic bricks; you built a subsidiary with worse margins.
The children get two seats while the electricity company gets a standing ovation.
Finally, a playground designed by someone who finds actual parks insufficiently technical.
That swing has more engineering behind it than the entire playground at your old elementary school.
The municipal parks department has declined to fund a playground for people made of bricks.

sticker buddy.text: A robotic future where even peeling a sticker requires an industrial support network.
The adhesive industry is delighted that its customers have started manufacturing their own complications.
NASA developed a robotic arm for space; this is the terrestrial version for stationery.
A sticker has somehow acquired a personal assistant before you did.
The label has a better onboarding experience than most new employees.

hello kitty.text: Sanrio manufactured an empire from a cat without a mouth; your printer is trying to replicate the business model.
Hello Kitty remains silent because even she knows better than to discuss the cost.
The only thing cuter than this cat is the fiction that the printer pays for itself.
A character famous for having no mouth has become the least argumentative member of the household.
Japan gave the world bullet trains and somehow this was the engineering export you chose to reproduce.

qr code.text: The future of information technology is apparently a barcode with a mortgage.
Congratulations on inventing a hyperlink that requires a power tool to relocate.
Your QR code has more physical infrastructure than the website it links to.
The digital revolution spent forty years escaping paper and you gave it a plastic pedestal.
Somewhere a restaurant menu is asking why its technological breakthrough suddenly needs a heated bed.

strandbeest.text: Theo Jansen harnessed wind power; your version specializes in harnessing the household checking account.
The Dutch invented a creature that walks along beaches and yours has to survive a carpet.
Evolution spent billions of years designing legs and the slicer still wants a support structure.
Darwin would call this natural selection if the credit card hadn't artificially intervened.
A mechanical animal that has already outperformed its creator at walking away from unnecessary commitments.

pinecone cottage lantern.text: Thomas Kinkade would ask why the cottage lighting budget exceeded the property value.
The woodland fairies have secured a mortgage through the electric utility.
That is an ambitious architectural project for a residence whose largest tenant might be a moth.
The cottage has managed to gentrify the forest without ever touching soil.
HGTV would renovate the pinecone and quietly triple the asking price.

triangle.text: Pythagoras discovered the theorem and somehow you discovered a way to charge admission.
Three sides, three angles, and a fourth dimension called unnecessary expenditure.
An isosceles triangle has two equal sides, unlike your income and your filament budget.
The Bermuda Triangle is famous for disappearing ships; yours specializes in disappearing afternoons.
The most acute angle in this project is the accountant's eyebrow.

sphere.text: A sphere has no edges, which makes it unusually difficult to corner the market.
Galileo went to trial over astronomy and you brought the jury a plastic ball.
The planet formed through gravity; your version needed a brim and a support group.
Archimedes would be thrilled that the surface area formula now includes a shipping charge.
The ball is perfectly qualified to roll away from any discussion of its purpose.

mobius strip.text: The Mobius strip has one side, much like the argument for buying more filament.
Mathematics invented an infinite loop and your printer found a way to bill it hourly.
A nonorientable surface for a hobby with an equally questionable sense of direction.
The topology is fascinating, especially the part where your spending comes back around.
This is the only strip of plastic that can show both sides without admitting there are two.

purge tower.text: The purge tower is the printer's version of building a guesthouse for the garbage.
Multicolor printing has finally perfected a method of making the packaging heavier than the gift.
The Statue of Liberty welcomes immigrants; your tower welcomes colors nobody ordered.
You've invented a chimney for a factory whose main pollutant is poor financial judgment.
The printer built a skyscraper for waste before developers could even finish the affordable housing paperwork.

build plate cleaner.text: Your cleaning equipment has a manufacturing lead time now, which should terrify the mop industry.
The build plate gets a spa treatment while the rest of the house waits for a vacuum.
A machine that cleans the surface on which you made the machine that cleans the surface.
The printer's janitor has a higher startup cost than the janitor's entire supply closet.
Even a Roomba would recognize the irony of producing more plastic to clean up plastic.

post it.text: Your sticky notes have finally acquired a filing system for reminders you will continue to ignore.
The invention of paper was insufficient, so the office supply cabinet requested a second Industrial Revolution.
The notes are now organized by color, urgency and the likelihood of being ignored.
A dedicated holder for the written evidence that you were supposed to do something else.
The sticky note has gained permanent housing while its message remains a temporary inconvenience.

mac mini.text: Apple made the computer smaller and you immediately started constructing real estate around it.
Steve Jobs removed every unnecessary component except apparently the one you just printed.
The Mac mini has acquired a custom apartment before the average software engineer can afford one.
Apple's minimalist design philosophy has been referred to your workshop for extensive remediation.
The computer is compact enough to fit anywhere except wherever you originally intended to put it.

ghost face.text: The killer in Scream had a phone; yours needed a slicer and several hours of electricity.
The horror movie budget was reasonable until someone decided the mask needed a matching caddy.
Ghostface has finally found a victim who willingly pays for their own torment: your wallet.
The sequel nobody expected is a slasher film about storage solutions.
Even a horror franchise with six sequels would question the necessity of this accessory.
